summary: Implements bridge mode VPN providers (Tailscale, Netbird), ACME certificate management, SNI-based routing, and tunnel providers (IPsec, OpenVPN) with comprehensive tests and documentation. All 24 tasks completed. Interfaces are well-designed and follow existing patterns. Security review found TunnelID injection risk and PSK-on-disk concerns that need addressing.

tests_checklist.item: V1: All tests pass (go test ./internal/bridge/... and ./internal/api/...)
V2: go vet passes with no errors
TE1: Happy paths tested with realistic data for all providers
TE2: Edge cases tested (empty keys, duplicate IDs, boundary ports, truncated SNI)
TE3: Error cases tested with specific error message validation
TE4: Tests independent with fresh mocks and no shared mutable state
TE5: Test naming follows Test<Type>_<Method>_<Scenario> convention
TE6: Mocking appropriate - only external deps mocked, integration tests use real components
TE7: Assertions specific - exact values, error prefixes, state verification
All interfaces have compile-time satisfaction checks (var _ Interface = (*Impl)(nil))
Mock test doubles follow existing pattern (mu, calls, per-key errors, callsFor)
Task 3.2: Serialization tests in internal/api/types_test.go for new fields

code_quality_checklist.item: P1: Follows existing error message convention (bridge: component: detail)
P1: Follows existing logging convention (component=bridge, structured slog fields)
P1: Config validation follows Validate() pattern (skip when disabled)
P2: Uses existing RouteController, VPNController, AccessController interfaces
P5: Files in internal/bridge/ matching project structure
Q2: Functions <=40 lines (some exceptions in SNI parser and config generation)

security_checklist.item: S1: Config inputs validated at API boundary (Validate method)
S3: No hardcoded secrets - auth keys read from env vars
S4: External commands abstracted behind CommandExecutor for testability
S5: Auth keys not logged directly (only key length logged for netbird)
S6: TLS MinVersion set to 1.2 in ACME and ingress TLS configs
S6: TunnelID not validated for path traversal before use in file paths
S6: PSK written to /tmp as plaintext config files

architecture_checklist.item: SNIRouter is self-contained with proper lifecycle management
SiteToSiteManager dispatches correctly between WireGuard and TunnelProviders
No new direct dependencies beyond golang.org/x/crypto (already existed)

dry_yagni_checklist.item: No unused code or YAGNI violations
IPsec/OpenVPN providers share structural similarity but not excessive duplication

fail_fast_checklist.item: Provider Start() fails fast on missing auth/setup keys
Tunnel creation fails fast on duplicate IDs
ACME Setup() validates cache dir and allowed hosts
SNI AddRoute validates hostname and backend address

defensive_checklist.item: All provider methods are concurrent-safe via sync.Mutex
Rollback on partial failures in CreateTunnel, AddTunnel, Setup

security_findings.description: S6: TunnelID used directly in file paths without validation. A TunnelID containing '../' or shell metacharacters could cause path traversal in config file writes (e.g., '/tmp/plexd-ipsec-../../etc/cron.d/backdoor.conf'). The TunnelID also flows into swanctl CLI arguments without sanitization.
security_findings.fix: Add TunnelID validation in TunnelConfig or at the SiteToSiteManager.AddTunnel boundary: reject IDs containing '/', '..', or non-alphanumeric characters beyond hyphens and underscores. Example: regexp.MustCompile(`^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$`).MatchString(tunnelID)

security_findings.description: S5: PSK secrets written to plaintext files in /tmp with 0600 permissions. While file permissions restrict access, /tmp is world-readable on many systems and files persist until explicitly removed. Config files containing PSKs are cleaned up on RemoveTunnel but remain on disk during tunnel lifetime and survive crashes.
security_findings.location: internal/bridge/ipsec.go:57 (generateSwanctlConfig writes PSK), internal/bridge/openvpn.go:59 (generateOpenVPNConfig writes PSK)
security_findings.fix: Use os.MkdirTemp with a plexd-specific prefix for isolation. Consider using a tmpfs mount point if available. At minimum, ensure cleanup happens via defer even on panics. Document the security trade-off if plaintext files are unavoidable due to strongSwan/OpenVPN requirements.

security_findings.description: S5: Netbird provider logs command output that may contain sensitive information. The output of 'netbird up' and 'netbird down' is logged at INFO level which could include auth tokens or network details in production.
security_findings.fix: Log command output at DEBUG level instead of INFO, or omit the output field entirely. Only log structured status fields (connected, IP, interface).

security_findings.description: SNI router has no read timeout on TLS ClientHello peek. A slowloris-style attack could hold connections indefinitely by sending data very slowly during the SNI peek phase.
security_findings.fix: Set a read deadline on the connection before the SNI peek: conn.SetReadDeadline(time.Now().Add(5*time.Second)). Reset it after successful peek.

architecture_findings.description: FC1: api.IngressInfo missing ACMEEnabled field. Task 3.2 specifies 'Extend api.IngressInfo with ACMEEnabled bool field' but this field was not added. IngressStatus() in ingress.go does not report ACME state.
architecture_findings.fix: Add ACMEEnabled bool field to api.IngressInfo and populate it in IngressManager.IngressStatus() based on whether m.acme is non-nil and active.

architecture_findings.description: Task 3.2 specifies serialization tests in internal/api/types_test.go for new fields (ProviderName, ProviderStatus, ProviderType, TunnelProviderNames, Hostname) but no changes were made to that file.
architecture_findings.fix: Add JSON round-trip tests for UserAccessInfo (with ProviderName/ProviderStatus), IngressRule (with Hostname), SiteToSiteTunnel (with ProviderType), and SiteToSiteInfo (with TunnelProviderNames) to verify serialization of new fields.

issues_found.description: TunnelID used in fmt.Sprintf("/tmp/plexd-ipsec-%s.conf", cfg.TunnelID) without validation — path traversal risk
issues_found.fix: Validate TunnelID with ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$ regex at SiteToSiteManager.AddTunnel or TunnelConfig level

issues_found.description: Same TunnelID path traversal risk as ipsec.go
PSK written to /tmp plaintext config file — survives crashes, visible in /tmp
issues_found.fix: Use isolated temp directory with restrictive permissions; document trade-off if unavoidable

issues_found.description: Command output logged at INFO may contain sensitive data
issues_found.fix: Log at DEBUG level or omit output field

issues_found.description: api.IngressInfo missing ACMEEnabled field specified in task 3.2
issues_found.fix: Add ACMEEnabled bool json:"acme_enabled" to IngressInfo; populate in IngressStatus()

issues_found.description: Missing serialization tests for new API type fields (task 3.2)
issues_found.fix: Add JSON marshal/unmarshal round-trip tests for ProviderName, ProviderStatus, ProviderType, TunnelProviderNames, Hostname

issues_found.description: No read timeout on TLS ClientHello peek — slowloris DoS vector
TunnelConfig fields (RemoteEndpoint, LocalSubnets, RemoteSubnets, PSK) interpolated into config files without validation — newline injection enables config injection in strongSwan/OpenVPN configs
issues_found.fix: Add validateTunnelConfig() that checks RemoteEndpoint is valid host:port, subnets are valid CIDRs via net.ParseCIDR, and PSK contains no control characters

issues_found.description: extractSNI function is 93 lines — complex TLS parsing logic
issues_found.fix: Consider extracting sub-parsers for ClientHello body parsing and extension iteration

issues_found.description: ~70% structural similarity between IPsec and OpenVPN providers (CreateTunnel, RemoveTunnel, removeTunnelLocked, ActiveTunnels, Stop)
issues_found.fix: Consider extracting shared tunnel lifecycle logic into a baseTunnelProvider or helper functions if a third provider is ever added

suggested_improvements: Add TunnelID validation regex at the SiteToSiteManager boundary to prevent path traversal across all providers
Use a dedicated temp directory (e.g., /run/plexd/tunnels/) for config files instead of /tmp to isolate secrets
Set read deadline on SNI router connections before TLS ClientHello peek to prevent slowloris
Add ACMEEnabled field to api.IngressInfo and populate in IngressStatus()
Add serialization tests for new API type fields in internal/api/types_test.go
Downgrade netbird command output logging from INFO to DEBUG
Consider extracting shared tunnel provider lifecycle code if adding more providers in future
